newsitem.title: USA: Cunanan's body released by Miami medical examiner.
newsitem.headline: Cunanan's body released by Miami medical examiner.

text.p: The body of Andrew Cunanan, the alleged killer of Italian fashion designer Gianni Versace, was released to a Miami funeral home for shipment to California, the medical examiner's office said on Sunday.
"We released the body yesterday to a local mortuary, Miami Memorial," a spokeswoman for the Dade County Medical Examiner's office said.
Calls to the funeral home were referred to Thurmond Wilkes at an affiliate company in Miami, Choice Cremation and Funeral Care, which will handle the shipping.
Wilkes said the body had been moved to an undisclosed location at the request of Cunanan's family and would be shipped later to the Glen Abbey funeral home in Bonita, California.

"The family asked that we keep things as quiet as possible," Wilkes told Reuters. "There is no arrangement as such. The funeral director who contacted me is off this weekend. It'll be next week before anything happens."
Cunanan is believed to have gunned down Versace on the steps of the designer's oceanfront mansion. He is also suspected in the killings of four other men.
Police found Cunanan's body on Wednesday after storming a housebout about two miles (3 km) north of Versace's home.

The medical examiner's office would say only that Cunanan died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound. It would not say whether he was already dead when police stormed the houseboat or whether he carried the AIDS virus.
There have been reports that his alleged killing spree was triggered by the discovery that he had tested positive for the human immunodeficiency virus that causes AIDS.
Dade County State Attorney Kathy Fernandez-Rundle said she would ask a judge to release the results of an AIDS test on Cunanan's body only if the information is deemed pertinent to the investigation.
"The law says specifically that it may not be made public," Fernandez-Rundle told television station WCIX in a Sunday morning news programme.
"We may never know the motive," she said.
